findings.title: totalPages calculation is off by one when user_count is an exact multiple of limit
findings.body: `totalPages` computes `Math.floor(this.get("user_count") / this.get("limit")) + 1`. When `user_count` is an exact multiple of `limit` (for example, `user_count = 50` and `limit = 50`), this evaluates to `2` instead of `1`. This causes the UI to display `1/2` and enables the `next` button, which then fetches an empty second page (`offset = 50`). It should be `Math.ceil(this.get("user_count") / this.get("limit"))` (or `Math.floor((user_count - 1) / limit) + 1`).

findings.title: alias_level is ignored when creating a group
findings.body: The `Admin::GroupsController#create` action sets `group.name` and `group.visible` from `params`, but never assigns `group.alias_level`, even though the admin group creation form displays the alias level selector and `Discourse.Group#asJSON` sends `alias_level` in the `POST /admin/groups` payload. Any alias level selected while creating a new group is silently discarded and reset to the database default.

findings.title: Adding an existing member to a group raises a uniqueness/duplicate key error
findings.body: In `Admin::GroupsController#add_members`, `group.add(user)` (`group.users.push(user)`) is called for each resolved username without checking whether the user is already a member of the group (`group.users.include?(user)` or `GroupUser.exists?(group_id: group.id, user_id: user.id)`). If an admin submits a username that is already in the group (or duplicates a username in the comma-separated list), inserting the duplicate `group_users` record will fail with a database uniqueness constraint violation (`ActiveRecord::RecordNotUnique`) and return a 500 error.

findings.title: Unbounded and unvalidated limit/offset parameters in GroupsController#members
findings.body: In `GroupsController#members`, `limit = (params[:limit] || 50).to_i` and `offset = params[:offset].to_i` are passed directly to ActiveRecord without bounds checking. A client can pass a huge `limit` (e.g., `limit=1000000`) to force loading and serializing all users at once, or a negative `limit`/`offset` which causes Postgres to raise an `ActiveRecord::StatementInvalid` (`LIMIT/OFFSET must not be negative`) resulting in an unhandled 500 error.

findings.title: Group members page fails to render members because GroupMembersController is an ArrayController
findings.body: `GroupMembersRoute` sets the `Group` model (a `Discourse.Model`, not an array) as the `model` of `GroupMembersController`, and this template was changed from `{{#each m in model}}` to `{{#each m in members}}`. Unless `GroupMembersController` is an `ObjectController` (in Discourse it defaults to/is an `ArrayController` when not defined as `ObjectController`), property lookup for `members` on the controller will not proxy to `model.members`, leaving the member list blank on `/groups/:name/members` (`model.members` would be needed or an `ObjectController`).
